cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul says the righteousness of God has been revealed, "…as attested by the Law and the Prophets." So this isn't a brand new idea showing up out of nowhere. The Law and the Prophets were already pointing at it, like a trail of crumbs leading to the cookie jar. Paul says they attest to it, friends, and that's the word to hold onto.

The answer is through faith in Jesus Christ. Paul says this righteousness from God "…comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe." Faith in Jesus is the way it comes, friends. Nothing else is listed next to it, and I checked twice.

The word is sinned. Paul says "…all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God…" Notice the word all, friends. Nobody gets skipped, and nobody gets to stand at the front of the line pointing at everyone else. That's why he says there's no distinction.

The answer is False. Paul says people are "…justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus." Freely means as a gift, so there's no payback plan hiding in the fine print. No invoice, no installments, nothing taped to the back, friends.

The answer is to demonstrate His righteousness. Paul says God presented Jesus as an atoning sacrifice "…in order to demonstrate His righteousness…" That's the reason he gives in verse 25. He repeats it in verse 26, so he clearly wants everybody to catch it.

The pair is staying just and justifying the one who has faith. Paul says God did this "…so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus." You'd think those two would pull in opposite directions, friends, like two cooks fighting over one oven. But Paul puts both in one sentence and doesn't make God pick one.
The answer is that it is excluded. Paul asks where boasting is and answers, "It is excluded." Just two words, friends. No pause, no maybe. He then explains it comes down to the principle of faith.

The blanks are works first, then faith. Paul asks, "On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith." If we earned it, we'd have something to brag about, and faith is the principle he names, bakers. I tried boasting about my own cookies once, and the dough just stared at me.

The answer is True. Paul asks, "Is He not the God of Gentiles too?" Then he answers, "Yes, of Gentiles too…" Gentiles are people who aren't Jews, and Paul says God is their God as well. He doesn't leave any doubt, friends.

The answer is that same. Paul says God "…will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith." It's the same faith for both, friends. No second, fancier version for anyone. One God, one way.

The answer is False. Paul asks, "Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith?" and says, "Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law." So his answer is no, friends. Faith doesn't do away with the law, it upholds it.
